title: Validate an opportunity
outcome: Know whether a record is real, current, and worth acting on.
steps: Open the organizer’s page—not a repost or search result.
Find the current date or deadline, eligibility, cost, and format.
Note what is still unclear and when the page was checked.
template:
Validation note
Official organizer:
Current date/deadline:
Who is eligible:
Cost/format:
Unanswered question:
Checked on:

title: Read eligibility without guessing
outcome: Separate a definite fit from a question that needs clarification.
steps: List your current enrollment level, credits, major, GPA, and transfer status.
Quote the exact rule that matters; do not paraphrase it yet.
Mark the result: eligible, not eligible, or ask the organizer.
template:
Eligibility check
My current status:
Exact published rule:
Evidence that I meet it:
Question for the organizer:
Decision:

title: Build a starter application packet
outcome: Create the reusable core of most applications.
steps: Prepare a one-page resume focused on evidence and results.
Save an unofficial transcript and list two possible references.
Draft a 150-word interest statement tailored to one opportunity.
template:
Starter packet
One-page resume: ready / revise
Transcript: saved / request
Interest statement: drafted / revise
Reference 1:
Reference 2:
Next deadline:

title: Ask for advice or a recommendation
outcome: Make a respectful, specific request that is easy to answer.
steps: Lead with the opportunity, deadline, and why it fits you.
Ask for advice before assuming someone can write a letter.
Attach or offer the official link, resume, and draft statement.
template:
Hello [name],
I’m considering [opportunity] because [specific fit]. The deadline is [date]. Would you be willing to advise me on [question]? If a recommendation is appropriate, I can share the official link, my resume, and a draft statement. Thank you for considering it.

title: Plan a local event visit
outcome: Turn attendance into learning and leadership.
steps: Confirm the venue, registration, transit or parking, and arrival time.
Choose one question to answer and one person or role to learn about.
Schedule a five-minute club debrief within three days.
template:
Event plan
Event and date:
Registration confirmed:
Travel plan:
Question I will answer:
Person or role I hope to meet:
Three takeaways to share:

title: Launch a competition team
outcome: Move from an interesting challenge to a realistic team plan.
steps: Confirm team size, eligibility, deliverables, and the real submission date.
Name a captain and assign research, build, documentation, and presentation roles.
Work backward to set a scope freeze, practice review, and final upload date.
template:
